slides.title: Not one lock, but layers
slides.text: The post office never trusts a single lock. A strong door guards the hall, a safe guards the parcels, and only Pim's key opens the safe. Three layers, one job.
slides.alt: Packet Post's title screen: Pim the owl at the Netville post office. Deliver every packet. Keep every secret.

focus.cue: Packet Post: the post office and its locks

slides.title: Updates patch holes
slides.text: When a game or tablet asks to update, it is patching holes. A hole is a small flaw a trickster could climb through, and the update sews it shut.
slides.alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.

focus.cue: The mailbox key builder, where one layer is made
The meter: how long a guessing computer would need

slides.title: Backups beat accidents
slides.text: A backup is a spare copy of your things, kept somewhere else. If a tablet breaks or gets locked by a trick, a safe copy elsewhere means nothing precious is lost.
slides.alt: A Good Spare Copy: the sorting round that tells a real backup, kept somewhere else, from a copy that is not.

focus.cue: A copy in the family's online folder
If the tablet breaks, which copies would save the day?

slides.title: Build your layer stack
slides.text: Pim is checking a home tablet before Spark Day. Tick each layer that should be guarding it.

slides.title: Two weak layers can win
slides.text: No single layer is perfect, and that is fine. Two ordinary layers together can beat one strong one, because a trick that slips past the first still meets the second.
slides.alt: A tablet holds messages and pictures. Signing out on a shared computer: does the habit protect it, or is it risky?

focus.cue: Signing out on a shared computer: one ordinary layer
A second layer still stands behind the first
